data.long_meaning: Sharo means 'sea' and Mitra means 'friend'. The name Sharomitra refers to the goddess who is a friend of the sea and is believed to protect and nourish it. The name Sharomitra carries the meaning “Goddess of the sea” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharomitra usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the sea and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine and the nurturing power of water. It is believed that this name bestows the blessings of the goddess of the sea and ensures the well-being of the individual.
data.etymology: Sharomitra belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the sea.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharomitra total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sharomitra holds a significant cultural importance in Hindu mythology, especially in the coastal regions of India where sea gods and goddesses are highly revered. It is believed that Sharomitra is a goddess who maintains the balance of sea life and ensures the prosperity of fishermen and seafarers. She is also regarded as the goddess of navigation and provides protection to all those who venture out into the unknown waters.

It embodies the idea of compassion, nourishment, and protection. Just as Sharomitra is believed to be a friend to the sea, we too can strive to be friends with all aspects of nature, recognizing that our actions have an impact on the world around us. Furthermore, the name also symbolizes the idea of seeking refuge and sustainability in the vast, endless expanse of the divine universe.
